title: Choose the plan your pieces can start
outcomes: Says which plan has a first move that exists in the position
Picks the move that starts a feasible plan
Rejects a plan whose first move no piece can play

steps.text: You already know a plan is a direction supported by a feature of the position (see *A plan the position supports*). Now you choose between plans. Test each one: **is there a piece that can start it, and does that first move exist right now?** A plan with no first move is only a wish. Pick the plan whose first move you can play.

A plan holds up when three things are true: the **feature** is there, a **piece** can carry it out, and the **first move** is available now. As a *rule of thumb*, if one is missing, prepare it or choose another plan. Where a capture or a threat decides the position, calculate instead; plans are for quiet positions.

steps.title: Same position, one pawn moved
steps.prompt: Only one pawn is on a different square. Predict which plan, if any, White can start, then check.
Before you answered, did you look for the first move of each plan, or only for the plan you liked? How sure were you? (low / medium / high)
